items.new_text: Find the shortcut matching current `de`/`ate`, if any; otherwise select Custom.

Survey scale follows metrics spec Section 6. Blip uses two incompatible market models without merging them; Pipe supports both but requires one type per survey and stores the scale with each response. Otherwise CSAT 4 and NPS 4 could enter the same chart. Type determines scale; do not allow manual scale entry that could create a 0-to-10 CSAT no report can classify. Keep this pure for the `'use client'` configuration card.
Expose metrics-spec Section 6 boundaries as text so the screen does not repeat numeric thresholds.
The database allows free text for survey trigger; this screen offers exactly three choices.

Classify a score within its type's scale for configuration preview. Keep this here, not `satisfacao.ts`: that report reads the class stored with historical responses, while this function shows what a new score WOULD mean before saving. Do not reclassify history.
Context offered by a newly arrived conversation to an entry rule.
Order rule evaluation deterministically by `ordem` then ID, as distribution spec Section 7 does. Without a tie-break, equal-order rules depend on unspecified Postgres row order.

Use the first matching active rule, or `null` so the conversation falls to the inbox default queue. An active rule with no conditions must never match: `avaliarExpressao` returns false for an empty list, avoiding an accidental universal catchall.
Describe a rule in full as the card displays it.

Identify unreachable rules by evaluation-order index. An active conditionless rule never matches; a rule below an identical earlier rule never wins. Surface both configuration mistakes so managers can understand why a tested rule has no effect.

Entry rules decide the destination queue (metrics spec Section 8). Blip docs leave two points open: evaluate ordered rules top-down and take the FIRST match; combine each rule's conditions with user-selected AND/OR exactly as displayed. If none match, `inbox.fila_padrao_id` selects the default, outside this module. Keep the module pure, without drizzle or `@pipe/db`, because a `'use client'` form imports it and DB code would pull `pg` into the browser. Evaluation delegates to `@pipe/core` (`score/motor.ts`) for identical operators, accent/case normalization, and dotted paths; a second Contains implementation would be a second rule definition.
Condition fields use first customer `mensagem` or contact data. `contato.atributos.` is a PREFIX, not a field; the suffix names a tenant-defined extra key such as `contato.atributos.plano`.
Label fixed or extra fields, including ones absent from the registered list.
Accept one of four fixed fields or an extra field with a nonempty key. Validate because a typo in a free field silently creates a rule that never matches and routes conversations to the wrong queue.
Use core `ROTULOS_PRIORIDADE` for Portuguese priority labels instead of a parallel map.

Priority rules supply the queue-edit section from `FICHA-atendentes-filas-pausas.md` Section a.3. `GET /v1/gestao/regras/prioridade` returns the whole tenant: `regra_prioridade` has `escopo_tipo` (`tenant` or `fila`) and `escopo_id`. Show only rules with `fila` scope and this queue's `escopoId`; tenant rules apply here too but are not edited in this section. Keep this pure (no `./api` or JSX) so `tests/regras-prioridade.test.ts` runs with `node --test` and `tsx`.
Keep rules for this queue in the API's existing name order.
Tenant-scoped rules apply to this queue too but cannot be edited here.
Return `erro.mensagem` from `api` `ErroPipe` or the default text.

A true REST write returns status 400/403/404/409 for `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`, unlike legacy `acoes.ts` `Resultado` with `{ok,erro}` in a 200 for `useActionState`. Match the per-call result shape in `paginas/fluxo/configuracoes/basicas/gravar.ts`.

Satisfaction report follows metrics spec Section 6. Store scale WITH each `resposta_pesquisa` score (`escala_min`, `escala_max`): CSAT 4 on 1-5 and NPS 4 on 0-10 mean different things. Group by type AND scale so incompatible scores cannot share a mean. Use the same closed-conversation period population for response numerator and rate denominator; mismatched populations would make the response rate meaningless.
Bar fraction divides counts; it is not a metric from the spec.
Surveys generated for conversations closed in the period, answered or unanswered.
Show responses divided by closed conversations in the period beside the average.
Response-rate denominator is conversations closed in the period.
Comment cap is a recent sample, not a full survey export.
Seconds beyond the SLA deadline when breached.

Detailed Monitoring SLA uses `@pipe/core` `avaliarSla` (metrics spec Section 11); this module selects the applicable rule and maps the result to screen text. Ponytail: the clock currently ignores working hours because `horario_atendimento` is not seeded, so no queue has a schedule to honor. `avaliarSla` already accepts hours; pass the queue schedule when available.
A queue-scoped rule beats a tenant-scoped one because the manager deliberately configured the more specific rule.
Import tokens and design-system base before the app stylesheet so local rules override the base.
Let the beam cover the whole window rather than one column: the reference right column is an illustration, while our artwork is the background; boxing it left half the screen blank.
Use our stroke for the reference button arrow (`arrow="true"`).

Welcome screen announces that the account was just created at login. Reference `#welcome-screen` places brand upper-left, centered text in a 40% column, right-aligned arrow button, and artwork in the right 55%, hidden below 1286px. Like the reference, this is a one-time gate: completed onboarding cannot revisit it even by URL. Keep forms on the next step so first entry is not an eight-field form.

Builder writes use `PUT /v1/gestao/fluxos/:id/builder` to save, `POST .../builder/publicar` to publish, and `POST .../builder/versoes/:versao/restaurar` for history. `api` owns rules in `dominio/gestao/builder-do-fluxo.ts`; here turn refusals into screen text and expose per-block engine errors from `detalhe.erros` on 409.
A publish refusal carries engine errors as well as a message.
Extract per-block errors from `api` 409 `detalhe` when provided.
Publish 409 can add errors to those already known from saving.
Show the `api` refusal message for read failures: 409 for router and 403 for missing permission. This is not Not found; the parent route handles 404.
Publish exactly what is on screen. Save first if changes are dirty or this is a new default flow; the Blip copy performs those two steps in order when publishing.
Explain why Publish is disabled in its tooltip.
Footer Saved status includes its underlying persistence state.

Builder layout follows captured production DOM (`referencias-blip/builder/builder-fluxo__pagina.html`; mapping in `builder.css`): notice strip, block-icon pill, dark canvas, status/zoom footer, conversation button. Pure `./builder/` modules `modelo.ts`, `condicoes.ts`, `conteudo.ts`, and `acoes-do-bloco.ts` edit the graph; `estado.ts` and `use-editor.ts` provide undo/redo and API-backed draft autosave; `canvas.tsx`, `no.tsx`, and `painel*.tsx` render graph and sidebar. Existing `/v1/gestao/fluxos/:id/builder` PUT saves a draft, Publish promotes it with per-block engine errors, history lists versions and restores an older one as draft. Unsupported frame controls remain disabled; confirmations use `Modal` from `cadastros/_modal`, never `window.confirm`. Route `/fluxo/:id/builder` stays inside the contact like source `/application/detail/<bot>/templates/builder`; `ESCONDIDOS_NO_ROTEADOR` in `fluxo/itens.ts` hides Builder for routers, and `api` returns 409 if opened by URL.

items.notes: pre-triage D-40; needs slice-time confirmation; scanner false-positive: URL in JSX href, not a comment; preserve URL bytes, remove inventory row before apply

items.new_text: Use `aplicar`, not `carregar`: imported flow must become dirty for autosave and undo, like any edit.
`carregar` only syncs server state and would leave an imported flow visible but unsaved.

Source icon pill `.builder-icon-button-list` follows captured DOM order: Add block, Builder Assistant, Publish flow, Configuration, Variable library, Search, Queue management, each `bds-button-icon variant="secondary" size="short"` with literal tooltips. Builder Assistant calls `$ctrl.createCopilotModal()`; with no AI provider in Pipe's engine, disable it like other unsupported controls.
Reference `.builder-footer` has a light status pill (Saved with `checkball`), three separate Undo/Redo/Fullscreen icons spaced by 10px, `100%`, and 100px slider from 20% to 100%.
Publish confirmation uses reference `bds-modal` and lists engine errors when refused; never use `window.confirm`.

Sidebar-pill button matches `bds-button-icon variant="secondary" size="short"` with right tooltip. Disable controls without an implementation by default and explain that state beside the control name.
When disabled, give a specific tooltip reason; otherwise say it is not built yet.
System-run actions belong to the Human block, not the person.
The engine does not execute this action: it throws at runtime and the conversation falls into the queue.
Create an action like the plus button: no title, empty settings, no condition.
Read `settings.a.b` case-insensitively because Newtonsoft matches keys without regard to case, and the screen must agree.
Write `settings.a.b`; empty text deletes the key.
Remove an empty nested object too; `context: {}` is not meaningful context.
Flow headers must stay objects; leave invalid text visible for validation instead of silently discarding it.
Point to the invalid field without erasing what the user typed.
Flow stores headers as an object; Builder edits them as key/value pairs.
Return missing action fields in panel wording; skip validation for actions the engine cannot execute.
Paste a full selection atomically or change nothing; copies must not share settings objects or IDs.
Move an action up/down in execution order.
A `settings` key may use a dot for nested keys, such as `context.type`.
`texto` is one line; `longo` uses a textarea.

Block enter/leave actions follow Blip editor Actions tab (`builder-tabs-actions`) but offer only what Pipe's `PROVEDOR_PADRAO` executes (`packages/core/src/fluxo/acoes.ts`). Add Tools offers `SetVariable`, `DeleteVariable` (Pipe label; absent from Blip's menu), `TrackEvent`, and `Redirect` with their Manipulate/Execute groups. `SendMessage`/`SendRawMessage` belong to block Content; `ForwardToDesk`, `LeavingFromDesk`, `CreateTicket` belong to Human and are created with it, hiding its Actions tab. Unsupported imported actions such as `ExecuteScript` or `MergeContact` remain readable and removable but marked Not executed in Pipe. Limit each action list to 15.

Global Actions in Configuration (`portal.js` `builder-configurations.globalActions.title`, `<actions state="$ctrl.globalActions">`) use the same `$enteringCustomActions` and `$leavingCustomActions` lists as a block, but for the whole flow. `editor.ts` confirms `globalActions.$enteringCustomActions` and `$leavingCustomActions` become executed flow-wide actions in published form. Reuse `acoes-do-bloco.ts` catalog, labels, and validation (`novaAcao`, `tipoDeAcao`, `valorDoCampo`, `comCampo`, `comTitulo`, `comCondicoes`, `errosDaAcao`); only list CRUD changes to `globais` (`Record<string, unknown>`) rather than `Bloco` with `id`.
Measure each card's actual height so its arrow leaves the correct edge.
Delete removes the selected arrow, or the selected block when that block may be removed.
Convert pointer screen coordinates to unzoomed canvas coordinates.
Find the block under the pointer in canvas coordinates; `elementFromPoint` can fail during pointer capture or with arrows overlaid.

Builder canvas mirrors reference `#canvas.grabbable` with scaled `#diagramContainer`: absolute blocks, SVG arrows behind, background drag to pan, Ctrl+wheel zoom by 10 from 20% to 100% like footer `rzslider`. Captured Pointer Events support mouse/pen/touch and keep drags outside elements. Block drag calls `onMover` repeatedly and `onSoltar` once for one `soltar` reducer step for undo; a click calls `onAbrir` like source `builder-node`. Drag from an output to another block calls `onLigar(de, para)`; dropping outside does nothing. Clicking an arrow selects it; Delete calls `onDesligar`, mirroring source `bind("click")` and `keydown Delete`. Right-click opens Duplicate/Copy ID/Delete except on Start. Measure card height after render so arrows leave the proper face as labels and titles change it.
Without real dragging, this is a click on the output point; do not create a self-loop merely from the click.
A Builder copy remains available even if the browser clipboard permission is denied.

Reference `condition-wrapper` for an exit or action lists If, source, variable, comparison, values in each row. All conditions must match; the engine stops at the first false one. Enter or comma adds a value tag, with OR/AND between values.
Changing the source clears a variable name that no longer applies.
Add one value on Enter; ignore duplicates and blanks.
Return `validarCondicao` engine wording or nothing when valid.
Pipe's engine has no AI provider, so intent and entity conditions can never match.
Add an exit with no destination and one empty condition.
Move an exit up/down in evaluation order; out-of-range positions do nothing.
Show exit errors using panel wording.
Label any source, including ones the screen does not offer.

Block-exit and action conditions use engine vocabulary (`packages/core/src/fluxo/condicao.ts`) and literal Blip Exit conditions tab labels (`builder-tabs-outputs`, pt-BR `sources`, `comparisons`, `and`/`or`). Offer only supported `input` and `context` sources, 13 `COMPARACOES` in enum order, and `or`/`and` among values. Blip `intent`/`entity` lack a Pipe AI provider: show an imported condition with a warning but do not offer creation. Exit order is evaluation order; the engine takes the first match (`FlowManager.ProcessOutputsAsync` ported in `gerenciador.ts`), then default. Provide up/down controls.
Read comparison as the engine does: case-insensitively, defaulting to `equals`.
New condition defaults to user response equals, matching the engine.
Changing comparison clears values when that comparison no longer needs them.
Render block `$contentActions` as cards in robot-send order.
Add content BEFORE user input: input remains last because the engine sends messages before waiting (`converterEstado` stores `input` outside the action list, while cards show the user's order).
Move a robot utterance up/down; user input stays last.
Change text and options of a menu or quick reply while preserving `scope`.
Replace a block's `input`; do nothing when no input exists.
Aguardar resposta enables waiting; Não aguardar maps to `bypass`. Create an input if none exists.
Return validation with a substituted rule and prefilled instruction, as the editor does.
Show block-content errors in panel wording.

Block Content tab follows Blip's conversation-like `$contentActions` cards, robot utterances left and user input right. Offer only Pipe channel `CONTEUDOS_SUPORTADOS` (`packages/core/src/fluxo/editor.ts`): text `text/plain` and two `application/vnd.lime.select+json` variants, Menu without `scope` and Quick reply with `scope: "immediate"`. Other Blip menu types (image, audio, video, document, sticker, carousel, HTTP, dynamic content, survey, location, web link, call request) are rejected on publish as unsupported `conteudo:<mime>`. Imported `chatstate` Typing appears but cannot be newly created and runs without effect. Limits match editor copy: 25 content items per block, menus up to 10 options of 24 characters, quick replies up to 3 options of 20 characters.
